claims.source_quote_ar: فهذا تنبيه على أن الأمر كله للَّه وعلى وجوب التوكل عليه.
claims.claim_ar: حركة بلاغية في الآية: الانتقال من بيان لينة النبي ورحمة الله إلى أوامر عملية (العفو، الاستغفار، المشورة) ثم الخاتمة بالأمر بالتوكّل؛ التنبيه يخدم ربط الرأفة بالطاعة والتسليم لله.
claims.claim_en: A rhetorical movement: the verse shifts from depicting the Prophet's gentleness and God's mercy to practical imperatives (forgiving, seeking forgiveness, consulting) and concludes with the injunction to trust in God; the admonition ties compassion to obedience and reliance on God.
claims.needs_review_reason: Inferred from thematic commentary (Zamakhshari/Darwish chunk) rather than an explicit label from the requested rhetoricians; needs comparison with classical balagha sources for precise taxonomy.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Emphasises that gentleness is compatible with firmness of purpose; moves the hearer from appreciation of mercy to concrete ethical instructions and final reliance on God.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار ضمائر المتكلم/الغائب (لهم/عنهم) في التركيب لتأكيد عناية الله بالناس وموضوع المسامحة واللطف في النص البلاغي.
claims.claim_en: Repetition (takrar) of the pronoun (e.g., لَهُمْ / عَنْهُمْ) in the structure to reinforce God's care for the people and the theme of forgiveness and gentleness in the rhetoric.
claims.needs_review_reason: The verse repeats the pronominal reference to the people (لهم … لهم/عنهم) — the exact pronoun forms in the commentary chunk differ ('عنهم' appears); the device identification is interpretive and should be checked against more explicit balagha discussion.

warnings: The provided source chunks are from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) and Darwish (I'rab). The task requested extraction from al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti and tafsir-balagha materials; those specific classical rhetoricians' chunks were not supplied.

Device assignments above are interpretative readings of the verse supported by the available commentary excerpts. For firm attribution to the classical balagha terminology (and higher confidence), cross-check with explicit discussions by the requested rhetoricians.

Some claims (pronoun repetition, surah-level movement) rely on thematic commentary rather than explicit labels in the source quotes; review by a subject-matter expert or with additional tafsir-balagha sources is recommended.
